Container.Name: NozzleWake

Branch.TagDescription: Latest build of the main branch

Container.Overview:
NozzleWake keeps inkjet print heads from clogging by sending a small maintenance print on a schedule (based on print-blockage-stopper by ahmedbadr3).
Features: multiple printers (the same printer can be added twice, e.g. plain and photo paper to exercise both blacks on Epson printers), "every N days" schedules counted from the last print, smart skip when the printer was recently used (including prints from other devices), low-ink alerts, Discord/Slack/ntfy webhooks, email and Home Assistant notifications, and a built-in dashboard.
Container.Description: Keeps any network printer's print head healthy by automatically sending a small test print on a schedule. Prevents pigment ink clogs without wasting ink on full cleaning cycles. Supports multiple printers, auto-discovery, custom test images, and smart scheduling. Works with Canon imagePROGRAF, Epson SureColor, HP DesignJet, and other IPP Everywhere compatible printers.
Container.Requires: Any network printer with IPP Everywhere support (usually any modern networked printer). Especially useful for pigment printers.
Container.Changes: ### 2.3.0 - Built-in ET-8500 maintenance pages: page 1 (plain paper: Matte Black, C, M, Y, Gray) and page 2 (Photo Black + Gray, A4 or 4x6), low ink coverage - Rename button on each printer card - Readable names for every paper type the printer reports; types that use Photo Black are marked - Larger printer-info line on full-size test pages ### 2.2.0 (NozzleWake) - Renamed to NozzleWake; image now ghcr.io/khaoq/nozzlewake - Webhooks work with Discord, Slack and ntfy directly (no proxy needed); several URLs supported; real errors shown by the Test button and in the log - Same printer can be added more than once; per-entry paper type (plain vs photo paper selects Matte vs Photo Black on Epson) - "Every N days" schedules counted from the last maintenance; no more back-to-back prints at month ends; failed runs retried next day - Smart skip uses the printer's own job history (prints from other devices) and matches plain vs photo paper - "Problems only" notification mode and low-ink alerts - Dark cyan dashboard theme and new icon - Security: fixed command injection via schedule, file read via test image, DNS rebinding, LAN access to CUPS printing/pausing, webhook SSRF and discovery-name XSS. New ALLOWED_HOSTS setting for access through a domain name ### 2.1.0 - Security: /api/printers no longer returns the SMTP password, Home Assistant token or webhook URL. If you ran an earlier version with any of these set, rotate them - Optional dashboard password (DASHBOARD_PASSWORD) protecting the dashboard and API - Unconfirmed prints are now cancelled instead of left queued, so they can't all print at once when the printer comes back - Offline printers are skipped; nothing is queued - Stale jobs are cleared before each maintenance print - Queue panel on each printer card: see waiting jobs, cancel one or all - Unconfirmed prints are recorded as failures, not OK - Alerts after repeated failures (FAILURE_ALERT_THRESHOLD, default 2) and when printing recovers - Completion wait raised from 3 to 10 minutes (JOB_TIMEOUT) - Built on the 1.5.x dashboard (supersedes the 1.6.0/2.0.0 React builds) ### 1.5.1 - Print completion monitoring — polls CUPS job status for up to 3 minutes - Detects stopped/held jobs (paper tray, jam, ink issues) - Distinct notification events: completed, stopped, timeout, failed - Input validation fixes (port, skip hours) - Fixed cron day-of-week parsing bug - PRINTER_ID path traversal prevention ### 1.5.0 - Email notifications (SMTP) — configurable from dashboard - Home Assistant integration — persistent notifications via HA REST API - Tabbed notifications UI (Webhook | Email | Home Assistant) - Test button for each notification channel - Unified notification dispatcher (notify.py) - Added GitHub README ### 1.4.1 - Next scheduled print countdown on each printer card - Custom test image delete button - Favicon for browser tab - New app icon - Security hardening (CSRF protection, XSS fixes, SSRF prevention, Content-Security-Policy) - Fixed chart alignment in print history - Fixed thumbnail not updating when changing test image - Replaced deprecated cgi module, use threaded HTTP server - CUPS config now persists across container restarts - Portable grep for broader Linux compatibility ### 1.4.0 - Inline printer rename (double-click name to edit) - Test Connection button with auto-detect printer model - Real-time connection status indicators (green/red dots) - Ink level bars (via IPP marker attributes) - Print retry logic (auto-retry once after 30s on failure) - Webhook notifications for print success/failure (Slack, Discord, ntfy) - CSV export for print history - Test image thumbnails on printer cards - Mobile-responsive layout improvements ### 1.3.0 - Multi-printer support (add/remove from dashboard) - Network printer auto-discovery (mDNS/IPP) - Per-printer status, schedule, and skip-hours - Preset test images for 4/6/8/11/12-colour printers - Custom test image upload (max 5 MB) - Smart skip: won't print if printer was recently used - Dashboard schedule pause/resume toggle - 30-day print history chart ### 1.0.0 - Initial release

Config.Name: Dashboard
Config.Description: Web dashboard for managing printers, schedules, and test images.

Config.Name: CUPS Web UI
Config.Description: CUPS print server interface for advanced monitoring.

Config.Name: Printer IP Address
Config.Description: (Optional) IP address of a printer to auto-add on first boot. You can also add printers from the dashboard after starting the container.

Config.Name: Default Print Schedule
Config.Description: Default cron expression for new printers. Can be customised per-printer in the dashboard. Default: every 3 days at 10 AM.

Config.Name: Default Paper Size
Config.Description: Default paper size for new printers (e.g., A4, Letter, A3). Can be changed per-printer.

Config.Name: Default Skip Hours
Config.Description: Default hours to skip maintenance print if printer was recently used. Adjustable per-printer in the dashboard.

Config.Name: Connection Type
Config.Description: Default connection type for new printers: 'ipp' (recommended) or 'socket' (port 9100).

Config.Name: Webhook URL
Config.Description: (Optional) URL for print success/failure notifications. Works with Slack incoming webhooks, Discord webhooks, ntfy.sh, or any endpoint accepting JSON POST.

Config.Name: Printer Port
Config.Description: Default port for socket connections (only used when Connection Type is 'socket').

Config.Name: Dashboard Password
Config.Description: (Optional) Require this password for the dashboard and API (HTTP Basic auth, any username). Recommended: the dashboard can change notification settings.

Config.Name: Allowed Hostnames
Config.Description: (Optional) Only needed if you open the dashboard through a domain name, e.g. via a reverse proxy: comma-separated names such as printers.example.com (a leading dot allows subdomains). IP addresses, single-word names (tower) and .local/.lan/.home.arpa names always work. Protects against DNS-rebinding attacks from websites.

Config.Name: Job Timeout (seconds)
Config.Description: How long to wait for a maintenance print to complete. Unconfirmed jobs are cancelled so they can't print later.

Config.Name: Failure Alert Threshold
Config.Description: Send failure alerts once this many runs in a row have failed.

Config.Name: Data / Logs
Config.Description: Persistent storage for printer config, logs, uploads, and CUPS state.

Config.Name: Unraid Notifications
Config.Description: Mount Unraid's notification script to get alerts on print failures. Leave default for standard Unraid installs.
